extensions.note: This is a React Native app. The component html/css below are faithful APPROXIMATIONS for the live panel, which renders web markup — the shipped components are RN StyleSheet objects in src/, not DOM. Treat the tokens and narrative as normative and the snippets as a preview.

primary.note: The one accent: active tab tint, primary actions, map pins, heart fills, app icon background. A light fill — white text on it is 2.64:1 and fails AA.

brand-subtle.note: Avatar fills and image placeholders before a cover loads.

brand-dark.note: Copper as text. The legible pairing on a Golden Hour Wash ground.

wine.note: The Insider star badge, and the Featured tier. Reserved — not a general accent.

teal.note: Reserved categorical. The Founding Pilot tier on the console.

navy.note: Reserved categorical. The org bundle tiers on the console.

background.note: The app ground. Warm by design — never #FAFAFA.

surface.note: Cards, sheets, tab bar. `card` is an alias of the same value.

text.note: Body text and the active pill fill.

text-muted-light.note: Placeholders and inactive glyphs only. 2.54:1 on white — never label text.

input-background.note: No console equivalent. Slightly warmer than Bone so a field reads as inset rather than as another card.

tab-bar-inactive.note: A warm gray, deliberately not Ash.

success.note: A fill and border tone. The console's text-safe success-ink variant does not exist here yet.

warning.note: A fill and border tone. On its own wash it is 2.14:1 — never type. The warning-ink variant does not exist here yet.

display-lg.purpose: The one big statement on a screen. Rare.

heading-sm.purpose: The most common heading; also the button label size.

caption.purpose: Tab labels, meta, timestamps. 11 is the floor.

shadows.name: shadowSoft
shadows.purpose: iOS resting lift on cards. Built from Graphite, not black, so it stays in the warm family.

shadows.name: shadowMedium
shadows.purpose: iOS sheets, floating map controls, and detached layers.

shadows.name: android-elevation
shadows.purpose: Android uses Material tonal elevation rather than these shadow tokens; 3 is the most common level in use.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Tactile press feedback. Currently NOT gated on a reduce-motion preference — both platforms require honouring that setting.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.value: supportsTablet: true on iOS, so iPad is a shipped device class with no dedicated layout yet

narrative.overview:
Golden hour is the short window near the end of the day when the light is best. Everyone who has chased it knows two things at once: it is beautiful, and it is about to be over. That is exactly what this app is for — the happy hour that is on now, and ends at six.

The palette is already named for it. Golden Hour copper is the brand, and the app is warm the way late light is warm: a bone-white ground, white cards, and copper used where attention should go. Where the console is an operator's room, this is the street outside it at 5pm.

The character is warm and glanceable at the same time, and that tension is the design problem, not a contradiction to be split. A venue card should feel inviting enough to want to go, and readable enough to decide in two seconds on a sidewalk. The resolution is hierarchy: time and distance are the fastest things on the card, the photography and the name carry the warmth, and nothing decorative competes with either.

Structure is the platform's, not ours. This app is recorded adaptive, and both HIGs govern navigation, controls and depth in every mode. Brand lives in the layer the platform leaves open: tint, type weight, motion, and content.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-neutral ground, copper for attention — the same palette as the console, token for token
Time is the fastest-read element on any surface that lists a deal
System typeface by design: San Francisco on iOS, Roboto on Android, no custom family
Platform-native structure and depth; brand in tint, type, motion and content
Pills for status and filters; soft 14px cards
Portrait only, light only — no dark mode exists

rules.name: The Golden Hour Rule
rules.body: Copper marks where attention goes — the active tab, the primary action, the live deal. One copper commitment per screen. Its scarcity is what makes a live happy hour findable at a glance.

rules.name: The Warm Gray Rule
rules.body: Every neutral here is warm. #FAFAF8 not #FAFAFA, #B5B0A8 not a cool gray for the inactive tab. A cool gray anywhere in this palette reads as a foreign component.

rules.name: The Shared Palette Rule
rules.body: These values are the console's values. A colour that changes here and not there is drift, not a mobile decision — change both or neither.

rules.name: The System Face Rule
rules.body: No custom font families. The brand is carried by colour, weight and voice. Adding a display face would cost Dynamic Type and platform metrics for a gain the brand does not need.

rules.name: The Scaling Rule
rules.body: Type scales with the user's system setting, everywhere, because nothing sets allowFontScaling={false}. Any layout that cannot survive a large type setting is the layout's problem, not the user's.

rules.name: The Ending Soonest Rule
rules.body: On any surface that lists a deal, the time it ends is the fastest thing to read. Not the venue name, not the photo. The whole product is 'what is on right now', and the layout has to answer that before anything else.

rules.name: The Platform Depth Rule
rules.body: Do not ship one depth model to both platforms. An iOS screen that leans on Material elevation looks like a port, and an Android screen with hand-rolled iOS shadows looks like one too. Depth is the layer where the adaptive call is most visible to a fluent user.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: 999 means 'this is a state or a filter' — chips, badges, tab pills — and also the primary button, which is the one place mobile deliberately diverges from the console, where pills are forbidden on actions. A full-radius primary button is native-feeling on a phone and alien in an operator console; both are correct for their surface.

rules.name: The Fourteen Rule
rules.body: The venue card is 14. It is the most-repeated shape in the product and the one a user sees hundreds of times; keep it consistent rather than drifting between 12, 14 and 16 on adjacent screens.

dos: Do answer 'what is on and when does it end' before anything else on a deal surface.
Do keep copper to one commitment per screen.
Do let type scale with the system setting, and design layouts that survive it.
Do use each platform's own depth model — flat and hairlined on iOS, tonal elevation on Android.
Do keep the venue card at 14px radius everywhere it appears.
Do use full pills for chips, badges and primary buttons on this surface.
Do take colour from src/theme/colors.ts. If a value is not there, add it there.
Do call background location 'Visit reminders' in UI copy, never 'background location'.
Do let people browse without an account, and replay a gated action after signup.
donts: Don't use stock palette values. #8B5CF6, #7C3AED, #60A5FA and #2563EB are currently in colors.ts under promoPremium* and promoBasic* — off-system, and carrying retired tier names.

Don't put white text on Golden Hour. It measures 2.64:1 and fails AA. The console flipped the label to graphite; mobile still ships the failing combination and has no brand-hover token to support the fix.
Don't set small text in a semantic mid tone. success, warning and error are fills and borders; the text-safe -ink variants do not exist here yet.
Don't add a custom font family.
Don't ship one depth model to both platforms.
Don't assume an in-app QR scanner exists — QR codes are read by the OS camera and arrive as universal links.
Don't design for dark mode. userInterfaceStyle is locked to light.
Don't design for landscape. Portrait is locked.
Don't imply offline capability. There is no offline layer; offline is empty states and errors.
